pages.raw_meta: TGS Announces Agreement with PetroGuin to Reprocess JAAN 3D Across Guinea-Bissau
raw_blocks: TGS Announces Agreement with PetroGuin to Reprocess JAAN 3D Across Guinea-Bissau

OSLO, Norway (15 October 2026) TGS, a leading global provider of energy data and intelligence, today announced an agreement with Empresa Nacional de Pesquisa e Exploração Petrolíferas E.P. (“PetroGuin”) for the rights to reprocess the JAAN 3D seismic dataset across Guinea-Bissau on a multi-client basis.

The agreement permits TGS to reprocess more than 11,000 km² of 3D seismic data, building on the parties' previous 2019 PSDM reprocessing. TGS will apply its advanced imaging technologies, including elastic dynamic-matching full waveform inversion (E-DMFWI) and Kirchhoff pre-stack depth migration (KPSDM), and expects a significant uplift in image quality compared with the existing data.

The improved imaging will enhance assessment of both clastic and carbonate targets across the margin, giving explorers greater confidence in their evaluation of prospectivity as they plan future exploration activity in Guinea-Bissau.
TGS will conduct the project in collaboration with GeoPartners, with reprocessing planned to begin in Q4 2026, and final products expected in Q4 2027.

Dr. Alfredo Malu, General Director at PetroGuin, commented, “PetroGuin highly values its longstanding partnership with TGS and reaffirms its commitment to fully honoring all obligations undertaken under this collaboration, in support of the sustainable development of Guinea-Bissau’s oil and gas sector.”

David Hajovsky, Executive Vice President at TGS, commented, “This agreement with PetroGuin allows us to apply our latest imaging technologies to a large 3D dataset across Guinea-Bissau. This reprocessing will deliver a clear step change in image quality, helping companies better evaluate both clastic and carbonate plays across the margin.”
The agreement was signed in person at the African Energy Week 2026 event in Cape Town.
EVP of Multi-Client, David Hajovsky with Dr. Alfredo Malu, General Director at PetroGuin, signing the agreement at African Energy Week 2026

pages.raw_meta: OSLO, Norway – TGS, a global provider of energy data and intelligence, in joint venture with SLB, announces the Pelotas Sul Phase 2 multi-client 3D survey offshore southern Brazil. The survey will cover approximately 11,200 square kilometers.
raw_blocks: TGS Announces Pelotas Sul Phase 2 Multi-Client Survey Offshore Brazil

OSLO, Norway (13 October 2026) – TGS, a global provider of energy data and intelligence, in joint venture with SLB, announces the Pelotas Sul Phase 2 multi-client 3D survey offshore southern Brazil. The survey will cover approximately 11,200 square kilometers.
A Ramform Titan-class vessel is scheduled to commence data acquisition in October 2026, with completion in Q2/Q3 2027.

Building on Pelotas Sul Phase 1, acquired earlier this year, the new survey will further expand TGS' high-quality 3D seismic coverage in a frontier basin that continues to attract industry interest. The Pelotas Basin is supported by geological analogs along the conjugate margin and de-risked by discoveries in Namibia. The basin offers a broad range of underexplored play concepts, including turbidite systems, deep-water channels, and stratigraphic and structural traps.

Pelotas Sul Phase 2 includes a balanced mix of held and open acreage. This provides data coverage relevant to companies evaluating existing acreage, while also creating opportunities linked to future licensing rounds and potential farm-in activity.

Kristian Johansen, CEO of TGS, commented: “Pelotas Sul Phase 2 builds on the strong foundation established by Phase 1 and further expands our coverage in a basin that is attracting growing client interest. The project will provide additional high-quality subsurface insight across both held and open acreage, supporting our customers as they evaluate existing positions and future exploration opportunities in the southern Pelotas Basin.”
For more information, visit TGS.com or contact:
VP IR & Business Intelligence

Kristian Johansen, CEO of TGS, commented: “The normalized Ocean Bottom Node (OBN) crew count in Q3 was 2.2, slightly above expectations.
